verses.1: The words of King David of Jerusalem.
verses.2: “Waste, waste!” said the voice that spoke. “All is waste.”
verses.3: What is gained by a person from all his efforts under the sun?
verses.4: The days go by, and the land remains standing forever.
verses.5: And the sun rose, and it came into its place. That’s where it was.
verses.6: It goes towards Darom, and turns towards Tzafon. It keeps turning around. The wind also moves around its surroundings. The wind returns to its original place.
verses.7: All the rivers flow towards the sea. And the sea isn’t able to hold them in place; they simply flow back again when they reach their destination.
verses.8: All these things are too difficult to understand. No one can speak about them; no one can even see them clearly. Nor can anyone fill their ears with sound.
verses.9: What would happen, and what would be done? There’s nothing new under the sun.
verses.10: There’s something that can be said: “Look, this is new. It’s something that has existed since ancient times, long before we came into existence.”
verses.11: There is no memory of the former ones, nor of those who will come after them. They will not have any memory of them either.
verses.12: I was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
verses.13: And I committed my heart to wisdom, so that it might serve as a source of comfort in all that happens under heaven. It’s a difficult problem that God has given to human beings, as a source of suffering.
verses.14: I saw all the things that were done under the sunlight. And I saw that everything was darkness and evil.
verses.15: Its defects cannot be repaired, and its lack of perfection cannot be corrected.
verses.16: I have spoken from my heart, saying, “I have grown in wisdom and knowledge over all that has happened before me in Jerusalem. My heart has seen much wisdom and knowledge.”
verses.17: And I decided to learn wisdom and knowledge of the divine. I realized that all of this is also a form of spiritual enlightenment.
verses.18: For in much wisdom there is much sorrow; and he who adds too much knowledge, will also suffer.
